nodes.name: Arrow bamboo
nodes.desc: Evergreen mountain bamboo that forms the understory. Wild pandas eat about 25 bamboo species, including Fargesia ones, so it underpins much of this web.

nodes.name: Farges's fir
nodes.desc: A conifer of the cool upper slopes. Conifer forest at higher elevations shelters the wildlife of the Qionglai range.

nodes.name: Hengduan Mountain oak
nodes.desc: An evergreen mountain oak recorded often around the area. Its acorns and leaves feed forest animals.

nodes.name: Father David's maple
nodes.desc: A broadleaf tree of the mid-elevation mixed forest; leaves and buds feed browsers.

nodes.name: Rose and shrub thickets
nodes.desc: A wild rose of the mountain scrub. Its flowers feed pollinators and its hips feed fruit eaters.

nodes.name: Festive bumble bee
nodes.desc: A bumble bee recorded often in the area. It collects nectar and pollen from mountain flowers.

nodes.name: Giant panda
nodes.desc: About 99% of the diet is bamboo. This site holds a large share of the wild population. Adults have few predators, but cubs and sub-adults can be taken.

nodes.name: Red panda
nodes.desc: Eats mainly bamboo leaves, plus fruit, blossoms and acorns. Leopards are its only documented predator.

nodes.name: Golden snub-nosed monkey
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating primate of the high mixed and conifer forests that moves lower in winter.

nodes.name: Sichuan takin
nodes.desc: A heavy goat-antelope that browses leaves and grasses and eats bamboo shoots and flowers. It retreats into thick bamboo when alarmed.

nodes.name: Forest musk deer
nodes.desc: A small, shy deer of the forest and thickets that browses leaves, shoots and lichens.

nodes.name: Yellow-throated marten
nodes.desc: An agile omnivorous marten that hunts small animals and may take panda cubs.

nodes.name: Asiatic black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats bamboo shoots, nuts and fruit and also meat. It can prey on panda cubs.

nodes.name: Himalayan griffon
nodes.desc: A big vulture that feeds on carrion of hoofed animals and is among the most often recorded birds here.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A top predator that takes deer, takin, monkeys and red pandas and may kill sub-adult pandas. One was camera-trapped near 4,080 m at Wolong.

nodes.name: Dhole
nodes.desc: A pack-hunting wild dog that preys on medium and large hoofed animals such as deer.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaches the understory through the canopy, so bamboo grows best where the forest opens.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain and mist
nodes.desc: Moist air from the Sichuan basin rises against the mountains, giving the wet climate that keeps the forest and bamboo lush.

nodes.name: Mountain soil
nodes.desc: Forest litter builds soils that feed the bamboo and trees across the steep slopes.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down leaves, bamboo litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
